analysis.title: Morning Report 18 November 2026
key_insights: Global equities sold off on a tech-led move. S&P 500 fell 1.5%, Dow 1.9%, NASDAQ 1.3%, Euro Stoxx 50 2.1%, FTSE 100 1.8%, Nikkei 1.3%, Kospi 2.6% and ASX 200 1.8%. Futures point to another weak ASX open.
Nvidia reports shortly after the report went to press. Westpac flags the earnings and any announcement on CEO succession plans as the next steer for sentiment.
US Treasuries bull steepened on weaker risk sentiment. The 2Y fell 5bps to 4.78%, the 10Y fell 3bps to 5.10% and the 30Y fell 1bp to 5.58%.
A December FOMC rate hike is fully priced, and a follow-up hike in January is seen as more likely than not. Fed speakers continue to support rapid tightening.

FOMC's Musalem called for "several" rate increases before spring 2027 to raise the real policy rate by about 1ppt. He described financial conditions as supportive of activity and the labour market as balanced and near full employment.

RBA minutes: members who dissented on November's rate hike worried the economy may be near a materially sharper downturn with costs in unemployment. Market pricing has no hikes or cuts fully priced through late 2027.
DXY pushed to a fresh cycle high just under 103.8 before easing to about 103.5. AUD/USD fell 0.1% to about 0.6730, a tentative stabilisation after a downtrend since early November.

Oil rose slightly on Middle East escalation: attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, an attack on US military equipment in Bahrain, and US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island described as self-defense. Brent rose 0.3% to US$92.7/bbl.
Metals were weaker with risk sentiment. LME copper fell 0.2% to US$13,226/mt and LME aluminium fell 2.3% to US$2,934/mt. Gold was broadly steady.

US October retail sales beat expectations: headline 0.2%, 0.1ppt above forecast, and the control group 0.6%, 0.3ppt above. Industrial production fell 0.4% and import prices rose 1.1% (0.8% ex-petroleum).
The NAHB housing market index fell from 29 to 25 in November, the lowest since 2011.
Euro Area ZEW expectations rose from 18.5 to 26.5 in November. UK ILO unemployment edged down from 4.7% to 4.6% and average weekly earnings growth slowed from 3.8% y/y to 3.6% y/y.
earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings due shortly after the report went to press (18 Nov 2026), with attention on any CEO succession plan announcement. No estimates are given in the report.
